summary.text: Defines the criteria for virological and immunological success or failure and for blood abnormalities, and describes the laboratory techniques used for CD4 counts, viral load and blood counts. It begins the results with patients' sociodemographic profile; the footer contains garbled text.

sections.title: Page 10

summary.text: Continues the discussion, comparing treatment efficacy with other countries and noting immunological-virological discordance. It discusses the limits of total lymphocyte counts as a CD4 substitute, attributes viral rebound mainly to poor adherence, and notes possible information and classification biases.

sections.title: Page 11

summary.text: Concludes that antiretroviral therapy is feasible and effective in Djibouti but that central structures and care of opportunistic infections should be strengthened before scale-up. Acknowledgements and the start of the reference list follow.

sections.extract: 1284 Conclusion Cette étude, portant sur la première cohorte djiboutienne mise sous traitement antirétro- viral, montre que le traitement antirétroviral est faisable et efficace à Djibouti. Avant son extension à l’ensemble du territoire, il est nécessaire de renforcer les structures centrales et la prise en charge des infections opportunistes.
